readings.title: Cain and Abel
readings.subtitle: The First Murder and the Line of Distrust
readings.text: [Genesis 4:1] And Adam knew Ḥawwah his wife, and she conceived and bore Qayin, and said, “I have gained a man from <dn1>YHVH</dn1>.” [2] And again, she bore his brother Heḇel. And Heḇel became a shepherd of flocks, but Qayin became a tiller of the ground. [3] And in the course of time it came to be that Qayin brought an offering of the fruit of the ground to <dn1>YHVH</dn1>. [4] And Heḇel also brought of the first-born of his flock and of their fat. And <dn1>YHVH</dn1> looked to Heḇel and his offering, [5] but <dn9>He</dn9> did not look to Qayin and his offering. And Qayin was very wroth, and his face fell. [6] And <dn1>YHVH</dn1> said to Qayin, <dq>“Why are you wroth? And why is your face fallen?</dq> [7] <dq>“If you do well, is there not acceptance? And if you do not do well, sin is crouching at the door. And its desire is for you, but you should master it.”</dq> [8] And Qayin told Heḇel his brother. And it came to be when they were in the field, that Qayin rose up against Heḇel his brother and killed him. [9] And <dn1>YHVH</dn1> said to Qayin, <dq>“Where is Heḇel your brother?”</dq> And he said, “I do not know. Am I my brother’s guard?” [10] And <dn9>He</dn9> said, <dq>“What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to Me from the ground.</dq> [11] <dq>“And now you are cursed from the earth, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.</dq> [12] <dq>“If you till the ground, it shall no longer yield its strength to you. You shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”</dq> [13] And Qayin said to <dn1>YHVH</dn1>, “My punishment is too great to bear! [14] “See, <dn12>You</dn12> have driven me from the face of the ground today, and I am hidden from <dn13>Your</dn13> face. I shall be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth, and it shall be that anyone who finds me kills me.” [15] And <dn1>YHVH</dn1> said to him, <dq>“Therefore, whoever kills Qayin, vengeance is taken on him sevenfold.”</dq> And <dn1>YHVH</dn1> set a sign for Qayin, lest anyone finding him should strike him. [16] And Qayin went out from the presence of <dn1>YHVH</dn1> and dwelt in the land of Noḏ, on the east of Ěḏen. [17] And Qayin knew his wife, and she conceived and bore Ḥanoḵ. And he built a city, and called the name of the city after the name of his son, Ḥanoḵ. [18] And to Ḥanoḵ was born Irad. And Irad brought forth Meḥuya’ĕl, and Meḥuya’ĕl brought forth Methusha’ĕl, and Methusha’ĕl brought forth Lemeḵ. [19] And Lemeḵ took for himself two wives, the name of one was Aḏah, and the name of the second was Tsillah. [20] And Aḏah bore yaḇal. He was the father of those who dwell in tents, with livestock. [21] And his brother’s name was Yuḇal. He was the father of all those who play the lyre and flute. [22] As for Tsillah, she also bore Tuḇal-Qayin, a smith of all kinds of tools in bronze and iron. And the sister of Tuḇal-Qayin was Naʽamah. [23] And Lemeḵ said to his wives, “Aḏah and Tsillah, hear my voice! Wives of Lemeḵ, listen to my speech! For I have killed a man for wounding me, even a young man for hurting me. [24] “For if Qayin is avenged sevenfold, then Lemeḵ seventy-sevenfold.” [25] And Adam knew his wife again, and she bore a son and called his name Shĕth, “For <dn2>Elohim</dn2> has appointed me another seed instead of Heḇel, because Qayin killed him.” [26] And to Shĕth, to him also a son was born. And he called his name Enosh. Then it was begun to call on the Name of <dn1>YHVH</dn1>.

readings.title: The Genealogy of Adam
readings.subtitle: Ten Generations from Creation to the Flood
readings.text: [Genesis 5:1] This is the book of the generations of Adam. In the day that <dn2>Elohim</dn2> created man, <dn9>He</dn9> made him in the likeness of <dn2>Elohim</dn2>. [2] Male and female <dn9>He</dn9> created them, and <dn9>He</dn9> blessed them, and called their name ‘Adam’ in the day they were created. [3] And Adam lived one hundred and thirty years, and brought forth a son in his own likeness, after his image, and called his name Shĕth. [4] And the days of Adam after he brought forth Shĕth were eight hundred years. And he brought forth sons and daughters. [5] So all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years, and he died. [6] And Shĕth lived one hundred and five years, and brought forth Enosh. [7] And Shĕth lived after he brought forth Enosh eight hundred and seven years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [8] So all the days of Shĕth were nine hundred and twelve years, and he died. [9] And Enosh lived ninety years, and brought forth Qĕinan. [10] And Enosh lived after he brought forth Qĕinan eight hundred and fifteen years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [11] So all the days of Enosh were nine hundred and five years, and he died. [12] And Qĕinan lived seventy years, and brought forth Mahalal’ĕl. [13] And Qĕinan lived after he brought forth Mahalal’ĕl eight hundred and forty years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [14] So all the days of Qĕinan were nine hundred and ten years, and he died. [15] And Mahalal’ĕl lived sixty-five years, and brought forth Yereḏ. [16] And Mahalal’ĕl lived after he brought forth Yereḏ eight hundred and thirty years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [17] So all the days of Mahalal’ĕl were eight hundred and ninety-five years, and he died. [18] And Yereḏ lived one hundred and sixty-two years, and brought forth Ḥanoḵ. [19] And Yereḏ lived after he brought forth Ḥanoḵ eight hundred years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [20] So all the days of Yereḏ were nine hundred and sixty-two years, and he died. [21] And Ḥanoḵ lived sixty-five years, and brought forth Methushelaḥ. [22] And Ḥanoḵ walked with <dn2>Elohim</dn2> three hundred years after he brought forth Methushelaḥ, and brought forth sons and daughters. [23] So all the days of Ḥanoḵ were three hundred and sixty-five years. [24] And Ḥanoḵ walked with <dn2>Elohim</dn2>. Then he was no more, for <dn2>Elohim</dn2> took him. [25] And Methushelaḥ lived one hundred and eighty-seven years, and brought forth Lemeḵ. [26] And Methushelaḥ lived after he brought forth Lemeḵ seven hundred and eighty-two years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [27] So all the days of Methushelaḥ were nine hundred and sixty-nine years, and he died. [28] And Lemeḵ lived one hundred and eighty-two years, and brought forth a son, [29] and called his name Noaḥ, saying, “This one shall comfort us concerning our work and the toil of our hands, because of the ground which <dn1>YHVH</dn1> has cursed.” [30] And Lemeḵ lived after he brought forth Noaḥ five hundred and ninety-five years, and brought forth sons and daughters. [31] So all the days of Lemeḵ were seven hundred and seventy-seven years, and he died. [32] And Noaḥ was five hundred years old, and Noaḥ brought forth Shĕm, Ḥam, and Yepheth.

readings.title: The Witness of the Chronicles
readings.subtitle: A Confirming Genealogy
readings.text: [1 Chronicles 1:1] Adam, Shĕth, Enosh, [2] Qĕinan, Mahalal’ĕl, Yereḏ, [3] Ḥanoḵ, Methushelaḥ, Lemeḵ, [4] Noaḥ, Shĕm, Ḥam, and Yepheth.

readings.title: The Corruption of Flesh
readings.subtitle: The Nephilim and the Ark
readings.text: [Genesis 6:1] And it came to be, when men began to increase on the face of the earth, and daughters were born to them, [2] that the sons of <dn2>Elohim</dn2> saw the daughters of men, that they were good. And they took wives for themselves of all whom they chose. [3] And <dn1>YHVH</dn1> said, <dq>“<dn18>My</dn18> Spirit shall not strive with man forever in his going astray. He is flesh, and his days shall be one hundred and twenty years.”</dq> [4] The Nephilim were on the earth in those days, and also afterward, when the sons of <dn2>Elohim</dn2> came in to the daughters of men and they bore children to them. Those were the mighty men who were of old, the men of name. [5] And <dn1>YHVH</dn1> saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually. [6] And <dn1>YHVH</dn1> was sorry that <dn9>He</dn9> had made man on the earth, and <dn9>He</dn9> was grieved in <dn11>His</dn11> heart. [7] And <dn1>YHVH</dn1> said, <dq>“<dn17>I</dn17> am going to wipe off man whom <dn17>I</dn17> have created from the face of the earth, both man and beast, creeping creature and birds of the heavens, for <dn17>I</dn17> am sorry that <dn17>I</dn17> have made them.”</dq> [8] But Noaḥ found favor in the eyes of <dn1>YHVH</dn1>. [9] This is the genealogy of Noaḥ. Noaḥ was a righteous man, perfect in his generations. Noaḥ walked with <dn2>Elohim</dn2>. [10] And Noaḥ brought forth three sons: Shĕm, Ḥam, and Yepheth. [11] And the earth was corrupt before <dn2>Elohim</dn2>, and the earth was filled with violence. [12] And <dn2>Elohim</dn2> looked upon the earth and saw that it was corrupt, for all flesh had corrupted their way on the earth. [13] And <dn2>Elohim</dn2> said to Noaḥ, <dq>“The end of all flesh has come before Me, for the earth is filled with violence through them. And see, <dn17>I</dn17> am destroying them with the earth.</dq> [14] <dq>“Make yourself an ark of gopherwood. Make rooms in the ark, and cover it inside and outside with tar.</dq> [15] <dq>“And this is how you make it: The length of the ark is three hundred cubits, its width fifty cubits, and its height thirty cubits.</dq> [16] <dq>“Make a window for the ark, and finish it to a cubit from above. And set the door of the ark in its side. Make it with lower, second, and third decks.</dq> [17] <dq>“And <dn17>I</dn17>, see, <dn17>I</dn17> am bringing floodwaters on the earth, to destroy all flesh in which is the breath of life from under the heavens. All that is on the earth is to die.</dq> [18] <dq>“And <dn17>I</dn17> shall establish <dn18>My</dn18> covenant with you, and you shall come into the ark, you and your sons and your wife and your sons’ wives with you.</dq> [19] <dq>“And of every living being of all flesh you bring two of every kind into the ark, to keep them alive with you – they are to be male and female.</dq> [20] <dq>“Of the birds after their kind, and of the cattle after their kind, and of every creeping creature of the earth after its kind, two of every kind are to come to you, to keep them alive.</dq> [21] <dq>“And you, take for yourself of all food that is eaten, and you shall gather it to yourself. And it shall be food for you and for them.”</dq> [22] And Noaḥ did according to all that <dn2>Elohim</dn2> commanded him, so he did.
